[Here's a TV ad](https://www.youtube.com/v/5A4v3vyHWOU) for Heineken Beer. In it, women are shown abandoning boyfriends/dates, who have had too much to drink. As the women take cabs and subways home, other drunk and passed-out men are seen in the background. The women sing the '80s pop song, *Holding Out for a Hero*.

where have all the good men gone?

where are all the gods?

The ad concludes with a man turning down a beer, and indicating to the bartender that he's done drinking for the night. The attractive woman bartender looks surprised. This guy is *different*. He's one of the *good men*. This guy, you see, is a *hero*.

So drink responsibly, guys ...because then women will notice that you're the hero they've been looking for. And maybe they'll touch your penis!

Look, I don't begrudge advertisers the use of sex as a gimmick to sell a product. They should do whatever works. Plus, it's not like Heineken can claim their product tastes good. So let's give them a break. It also doesn't bother me that the ad is a quintessential blue-pill lie - the kind of lie that takes the form, "here's how you get women."

The truth is, being a responsible drinker is not going to make women attracted to you, even if being drunk is **un**attractive. Not being unattractive is not the same thing as being attractive, in the same way that not being in debt is not the same thing as being rich. Women might be turned off by drunkenness, but that's only because they're turned off by weakness. Amy Winehouse [has an actual, honest take on this principle](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7CYE0DYIbaw). "You should be stronger than me" she sings. Not being weak is not the same thing as being strong. But I digress...

The reason I post this here is not that it's a cringe-worthy use of sex to sell a product, and not that it's a lie about human sexuality. The reason I post this is to have you consider a gender-flipped version of the ad. Imagine telling women to drink responsibly. Imagine telling women to take responsibility for ...well, anything! Imagine an ad featuring [a hot drunk girl attacking an uber driver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-otd29xd0UU) and imagine a man walking away while singing:

where have all the virtuous women gone?

where are all the ladies?

If you're a lurker here at /v/MGTOW and this prospect rustles your jimmies, then I invite you to post an example of an ad whose message is that women aren't being responsible, particularly to men, but they should be. When you can't do that, be honest and admit that no such ad exists, because that message would be incredibly offensive.

My point is **not** that the Heineken ad is offensive to me. At its core, it's good advice. I'll even repeat it: guys, drink responsibly! A DUI, or even just getting mugged, isn't worth it.

No, my point, for my MGTOW brothers, is that the difference between the way this ad is perceived, and the way a gender-flipped ad would be perceived, demonstrates what society thinks of you. I'm advising you to drink responsibly *for yourself*, because a DUI would be bad *for you*. The rest of the world tells you to drink responsibly *for women*, because you're supposed to be useful to them. You owe them that, but they don't owe you anything.

This is the kind of shit that makes men say "fuck you" and go our own way.

Back to the ad, at 0:14 a woman is shown getting her date's coat from a coat-check. She takes the keys to his car, and tosses the coat over his slouching, passed-out body. Presumably, she then drives his car home, leaving him there. If it was her car too (as in, they were married), she'd have her own key. So yeah, there's an ad on TV right now that suggests it's okay to steal a guy's car. Isn't that nice?
